record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Fix a transfer function that admits positive minimal realizations. How are all of its positive minimal realizations related to one another? For example, can one describe the structure or transformations that connect any two minimal positive realizations of the same system?

evidence.quote: - how are all positive minimal realizations connected?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A single-input single-output linear time-invariant discrete-time system is called positive if its state, input and output remain in the nonnegative orthant for all nonnegative inputs and nonnegative initial states. A positive realization of a rational transfer function $H(z)$ is a quadruple $(A,b,c,d)$ with $A\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{n\times n}$, $b\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{n}$, $c\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{1\times n}$, $d\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ satisfying $H(z)=d+c(zI-A)^{-1}b$. Such a positive realization is called minimal if its state-space dimension $n$ is the smallest possible among all positive realizations of $H(z)$ (note that this minimal positive dimension may strictly exceed the McMillan degree of $H$).

Fix a rational transfer function $H(z)$ that admits at least one minimal positive realization, and let $n$ denote the minimal positive dimension. Characterize the set of all minimal positive realizations of $H(z)$: describe explicitly the group, semigroup, or family of admissible transformations $(A,b,c,d)\mapsto(\tilde A,\tilde b,\tilde c,\tilde d)$ that takes any minimal positive realization to any other, and determine the structure (e.g., connectedness, orbit decomposition) of this set in $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{n\times n}\times\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{1\times n}\times\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and papers (e.g., a 2022 Automatica survey on minimal positive realizations and 2025 work on minimal positive Markov realizations) continue to list the characterization of minimality and the relationship among different minimal positive realizations of the same transfer function as unsolved. No general structural theorem connecting arbitrary minimal positive realizations is known; the problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive realizations: A survey (Automatica, 2022)
status_evidence.snippet: The characterization of minimality for positive systems is still an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Characterizing minimality, and thus how minimal positive realizations relate, remains open.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive Markov realizations (arXiv:2502.21102)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies minimal positive realizations in a Markov setting; references the still-open general minimality/classification problem.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work continues to treat the classification of minimal positive realizations as open.
